page: Vultr voc-g-1c-4gb-30s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring a single dedicated AMD EPYC vCPU running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory and 30 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not feature any GPU hardware. The CPU configuration consists of one physical core and one thread, with a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and FMA.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% of stress-ng benchmarks, and Geekbench single-core performance is average. However, due to the single-vCPU limitation, multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench is poor, falling into the bottom 10% to 25%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only small block cached bandwidth rated as poor at 142.91 GB/sec, and uncached large block read and write speeds categorized as weak. Text processing and single-threaded compression tasks perform at average levels, while database operations, static web serving, and software compilation benchmarks score in the lower percentiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a dedicated CPU allocation and NVMe storage at an entry-level resource density, making it a viable option for workloads that require predictable single-core performance without the overhead of shared-core resource contention. Given its hardware constraints, the instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, simple web serving, and development or testing environments that do not require parallel processing or high memory bandwidth.
